title: Option Type Intro
story: You're building a contact search for your phone app. When someone searches for a name, sometimes you find a match — and sometimes there's nothing. You need a type that says 'I have something' or 'I have nothing.'
why: The Option pattern handles 'maybe there's a value' situations — it's safer than using a special number (like -1) to mean 'not found.'
analogy: Option is like looking in a drawer — either you find something (Some with the item) or the drawer is empty (None). There's no confusing a real found item with the absence of an item.
try_it: Add a third player "Dana" with score 72. Test finding Dana. Then write a `best_score` function that takes two MyOptions and returns the higher score (or 0 if both are None).
tips: `None` has no parentheses — it's a simple variant like `Sunny`
Always match both `Some` and `None` — the compiler won't let you forget the empty case
Use Option instead of special values like -1 to mean 'not found' — it's clearer and safer
common_mistakes: Writing `MyOption.Some()` with no argument — `Some` requires a value: `MyOption.Some(42)`
Forgetting that `None` has its own arm in match — it's a variant like any other
Returning just `Some(value)` without the enum prefix — must write `MyOption.Some(value)`
